html:
Hanthawaddy was a kingdom of the Mon in Lower Burma from 1287 to 1539, with its capital at Pegu (Bago) from 1369. It was the richest state in Burma in that age, thanks to sea trade.

Its ports traded with India, Malacca and the Arab world. Queen Shin Sawbu and her successor Dhammazedi in the 15th century were great builders and patrons of Buddhism; they raised the Shwedagon Pagoda to near its present height.

Hanthawaddy fought the Burman kingdom of Ava for forty years. It fell to Taungoo in 1539, and Pegu became the capital of Bayinnaung. Mon revolts revived it briefly in the 18th century until Alaungpaya crushed it.
